caption: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, Disjunctive Reasoning, and Conjunctive Reasoning.
model_annotation: The image displays three pie charts illustrating the distribution of quantifiers and operations across three distinct reasoning categories from the R2I-Bench benchmark: “Categorical,” “Approximate Number Generation,” and “Disjunctive & Conjunctive.” The first chart, “Categorical,” is divided into four segments: “Existential Quantifiers” (15.12%, light green), “Limiter” (27.91%, light pink), “Negation” (27.91%, light orange), and “Universal Quantifiers” (29.07%, light blue), with the latter being the largest segment. The second chart, “Approximate Number Generation,” contains three segments: “Absolute Absence” (18.71%, lavender), “Approximate Quantities” (45.03%, beige), and “Comparative Relationships” (36.26%, light blue), where “Approximate Quantities” dominates. The third chart, “Disjunctive & Conjunctive,” is split nearly evenly into two halves: “Disjunctive” (49.51%, light lavender) and “Conjunctive” (50.49%, light purple), with the “Conjunctive” segment being marginally larger. All charts include percentage labels within each slice and use distinct pastel colors for visual differentiation, with no legend provided. The segments in each pie chart are ordered clockwise from the top, though not necessarily by size.
